claims.head: The matchup inside the matchup
claims.body: The Rangers are one of the league’s best for the power play, and the Lightning are near the top of the league at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Rangers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
claims.call: The Rangers’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.5 expected goals per 60 against the Lightning.
claims.nums: NY Rangers 5th for the power play (8.4 expected goals per 60) · Tampa Bay 8th for the penalty kill
claims.gist: It’s strength against strength: the Rangers for the power play, the Lightning at the penalty kill.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 6 and 4 games this season

check.measure: expected goals per 60 on the power play
check.rule: held if tonight's figure lands on the predicted side of the league average; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Rangers will send their checkers at Guentzel
claims.call: The Rangers’ L2 (Miller, Dorofeyev and Kartye) spends at least 42% of its 5-on-5 time against the Lightning’s first line.
claims.body: At home, the Rangers keep sending Dorofeyev’s line (Miller, Dorofeyev and Kartye) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would. That’s a checking assignment: Mike Sullivan wants this group on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Lightning’s first line is Guentzel, Cirelli and Hagel.
claims.nums: At home: 42% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 29% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Mike Sullivan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Lightning’s first line.

claims.head: Volume against patience
claims.body: On shot volume, Tampa Bay is one of the league’s best and the Rangers is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
claims.nums: Shot volume: Tampa Bay 4th, NY Rangers 28th
claims.gist: The Lightning and the Rangers sit at opposite ends for shot volume.
claims.call: The Lightning take more 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than the Rangers.

NYR.body: Tampa Bay has controlled the play far better over recent games and the Rangers have home ice. The Rangers’ best way through is pouncing on loose pucks.
